items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew by 25% year-on-year to Rs 9,370 crores during the first quarter despite operating volatility.
items.quote: Consolidated Revenues for the April – June 2026 quarter were Rs 60,794 crores and EBITDA was Rs 9,370 crores. EBITDA improved by 25% YoY despite the volatile operating environment.

items.statement: Tata Steel UK reduced its EBITDA loss sequentially to £27 million, supported by improvement measures and pricing.
items.quote: Within our overseas portfolio, UK narrowed its EBITDA loss from -ve £48 million in 4Q to -ve £27 million in 1Q, reflecting the impact of targeted improvement initiatives and better pricing supported by trade measures.

items.statement: Working capital was negatively impacted by higher prices and inventory accumulation resulting from operational and supply chain bottlenecks.
items.quote: Working capital was impacted by inventory build due to operational and supply chain disruptions, and an increase in prices. We remain focused on cost optimisation and working capital efficiency to maximise cashflows.

items.statement: Operational and financial results in the Netherlands were hurt by the shutdown of the Direct Sheet Plant.
items.quote: Netherlands revenues were €1,445 million for the quarter and EBITDA was €4 million. Liquid steel production was 1.55 million tons and deliveries were 1.40 million tons, with operations affected by the closure of the Direct Sheet Plant.

items.statement: Management expects production and delivery volumes in India to return to normal in the upcoming quarters.
items.quote: Quarterly production and deliveries were affected by maintenance shutdowns in Meramandali and Kalinganagar. Production and deliveries are expected to normalise in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Safeguard measures implemented in the UK are anticipated to provide a supportive market environment across products.
items.quote: In UK, the recently implemented safeguard measures are expected to provide a more supportive market environment, although the benefits vary across product categories. We continue to engage with the UK government to support a level playing field for domestic producers.

items.statement: Tata Steel maintained a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 2.3x, staying below its through-the-cycle guidance range of 2.5x to 3.0x.
items.quote: Net debt stood at Rs 84,173 crores and Net debt to EBITDA was 2.3x, below our stated range of 2.5 - 3.0x through cycle.

items.statement: Indian apparent steel demand grew during the quarter even as steel imports exceeded exports.
items.quote: India apparent steel demand continued to grow, but imports outpaced exports during the quarter Govt has initiated anti dumping investigation on Hot Rolled steel imports from select countries

items.statement: Tata Steel's branded steel offerings continue to see strong demand in the retail long products sector.
items.quote: This will enable Tata Steel to further expand the long products portfolio especially in the retail space where our branded products are in high demand.

items.statement: Agile commercial strategies helped drive a quarter-on-quarter increase of Rs 5,991 per ton in net steel realisations.
items.quote: Our agile commercial strategy and calibrated market mix enabled us to maximise value realisation across segments, driving a strong QoQ improvement of Rs 5,991 per ton in net steel realisations.

items.statement: Geopolitical unrest in West Asia aggravated input cost inflation and disrupted supply chains during the quarter.
items.quote: Global operating environment remained complex, with the impact of developments in West Asia on supply chains and input costs being more pronounced in the quarter. Our overseas operations also had to navigate operational disruptions.

items.statement: Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited achieved an EBITDA margin of 29% on EBITDA of Rs 498 crores.
items.quote: Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, our strategic platform for expanding the long products portfolio, generated EBITDA of Rs 498 crores, which translates to a robust margin of 29%, and provides confidence for the expansion project.

items.statement: Tata Steel deployed Rs 3,579 crores toward capital expenditure during the quarter.
items.quote: The company has spent Rs 3,579 crores on capital expenditure during the quarter.

items.statement: The board approved a capital expenditure of Rs 33,873 crores for expanding steelmaking capacity at Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited.
items.quote: The Board has approved the core project of steelmaking capacity expansion by 4.8 MTPA in Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited at an estimated capex of Rs 33,873 crores.

items.statement: Ramping up of the Ludhiana EAF is underway along with progress on the pickling and galvanising line and tinplate expansions.
items.quote: Our 0.75 MTPA EAF at Ludhiana is ramping up and construction is in progress for the 0.7 MTPA Hot Rolled Pickling & Galvanising Line, along with Phase 1 expansion of Tinplate from 0.4 to 0.7 MTPA.

items.statement: A board-approved 4.8 MTPA expansion at Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited will take its total capacity to 6.2 MTPA.
items.quote: The Board has approved ~Rs 33,873 crores towards the core project of steelmaking capacity expansion by 4.8 MTPA at Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, which will expand the total capacity to 6.2 MTPA.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt stood at Rs 84,173 crores with group liquidity maintained at Rs 45,950 crores.
items.quote: Net debt stood at Rs 84,173 crores and Net debt to EBITDA was 2.3x. Our group liquidity remains strong at Rs 45,950 crores, which includes cash & cash equivalents of Rs 13,221 crores.

items.statement: Tata Steel UK is undertaking a project to transition to a scrap-based 3 MTPA Electric Arc Furnace.
items.quote: In UK, transition to scrap-based EAF steelmaking to reduce 50 million tons CO2e over a decade EAF project update EAF project – Transition to scrap based Electric Arc Furnace of around 3 MTPA capacity

items.statement: Tata Steel expanded into the container and data center industries, supplying steel for dry fit containers and two projects.
items.quote: Making inroads into Data Centre, catered 2 projects in Maharashtra during Apr – Jun’26 quarter Entry into Container segment with high tensile steel supply for ~500 Dry Fit containers

items.statement: Tighter steel import safeguard quotas were enacted in both the European Union and the UK effective July 1, 2026.
items.quote: EU and UK have incorporated tighter safeguard quotas effective 01st July 2026 However, in UK there were deviations from initial proposal, with implications for product categories

items.statement: Indian steel demand is outpacing domestic GDP growth while per capita steel usage remains below the global average.
items.quote: India steel demand growth higher than the GDP growth rate 100 kg India steel use per capita lower than global average of 215 kg per capita

items.statement: Shifting economic conditions that alter demand, supply, and pricing in domestic and international markets are key operating risks.
items.quote: Important factors that could make a difference to the Company’s operations include, among others, economic conditions affecting demand / supply and price conditions in the domestic and overseas markets in which the Company operates

items.statement: positive
items.quote: Quarterly production and deliveries were affected by maintenance shutdowns in Meramandali and Kalinganagar. Production and deliveries are expected to normalise in the coming quarters.

items.statement: In the first quarter of FY27, India EBITDA rose 32% year-on-year to approximately Rs 9,900 crores, with EBITDA per ton increasing to Rs 19,162.
items.quote: In 1QFY27, India EBITDA was higher by 32% YoY to about Rs. 9,900 crores. India continues to deliver industry-leading margins. EBITDA per ton improved significantly from about Rs. 15,907 per ton in 4Q to about Rs. 19,162 per ton in 1Q.

items.statement: UK revenues rose 3% quarter-on-quarter to roughly £484 million, supported by a £91 per ton increase in net realisations.
items.quote: UK revenues stood at about £484 million, an increase of 3% or £15 million on QoQ basis, despite a drop in volumes. The uplift was driven by higher net realisations to the tune of about £91 per ton.

items.statement: Stand-alone revenue gains were partly offset by a cost increase of around Rs 6,700 per ton due to lower volumes, scheduled shutdowns, and operational issues.
items.quote: Total revenue was up by about Rs. 9,212 per ton. However, this was partly offset by the rise in cost by about Rs. 6,700 per ton due to lower volumes during the quarter, due to annual shutdowns and operational snags

items.statement: A major fire occurred at the Port Talbot pickle line on June 3, 2026, though all workers were evacuated safely.
items.quote: On 03rd June 2026, there was a major fire at the Port Talbot pickle line. All personnel were safely evacuated with no injuries, reflecting strong safety protocols.

items.statement: The company expects steel realisations in India to drop by approximately Rs 1,500 per ton in the second quarter compared to the first quarter.
items.quote: This quarter, we are saying will be about Rs 1,500 per ton lower than 1Q in India. Obviously, some areas like in long products, the drop between April and July is much more than in flat products.

items.statement: Tata Steel anticipates UK steel prices to rise by another £70 to £80 per ton in the second quarter over the first quarter.
items.quote: And as far as 2Q is concerned, it will be another £70 – £80 per ton increase is what we are expecting in 2Q over 1Q. But all of it doesn't flow to the margins because UK is fed out of substrate.

items.statement: Capital expenditure during the quarter stood at approximately Rs 3,579 crores, with the majority spent in India.
items.quote: Moving now to cash flows, we spent about Rs. 3,579 crores on capital expenditure during the quarter, of which the majority was in India.

items.statement: The Board approved an investment of Rs 33,873 crores for a 4.8 MTPA long products capacity expansion at NINL.
items.quote: Board yesterday accorded the final investment approval for the 4.8 MTPA expansion in long products capacity covering wire rods and rebars, including solutions beyond that, at the NINL site for an investment of Rs. 33,873 crores

items.statement: A 0.3 MTPA tinplate expansion and a 0.74 MTPA hot roll pickling and galvanising project are scheduled for completion within 30 months.
items.quote: The 0.3 MTPA capacity expansion in tinplate and the hot roll pickling and galvanising project of 0.74 MTPA are both on track for completion within the next 30 months.

items.statement: The company commissioned a 0.5 MTPA combi mill in Jamshedpur and aims to add 0.42 million tonnes of tube capacity during FY2027.
items.quote: The 0.5 MTPA combi mill in Jamshedpur has been commissioned and is midway through its ramp up. We plan to add about 0.42 million tons of tube capacity also during FY2027 through an asset light model.

items.statement: Net debt stood at around Rs 84,000 crores, resulting in a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 2.3x.
items.quote: On the balance sheet, net debt stands at about Rs. 84,000 crores and the net debt to EBITDA is comfortably at 2.3x, which is within our stated range of 2.5 to 3x through the cycle.

items.statement: Group liquidity remained strong at about Rs 45,950 crores, which includes Rs 13,221 crores in cash and cash equivalents.
items.quote: Our group liquidity remains strong at about Rs. 45,950 crores, which includes about Rs. 13,221 crores of cash and cash equivalents. This provides significant financial flexibility to fund our growth and our upcoming projects.

items.statement: The company developed cold rolled ultra-high tensile steel DP980 for commercial vehicles alongside specialty coatings for passenger vehicles.
items.quote: We also developed cold rolled ultra-high tensile steel DP980, for those of you who understand the technicality of it for commercial vehicles and galvannealed steel and secondary coatings for passenger vehicles

items.statement: Material costs increased by approximately Rs 1,330 per ton and conversion costs increased by around Rs 5,400 per ton quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: Within costs, material costs were up by about Rs. 1,330 per ton and conversion costs were up by about Rs. 5,400 per ton on QoQ basis.

items.statement: Coking coal consumption costs in the second quarter are projected to rise by $5 per ton in India and $10 per ton in the Netherlands.
items.quote: So, the consumption cost in 2Q for coking coal in India will be about $5 per ton higher, and for Netherlands will be about $10 per ton higher.

items.statement: Higher realisations of Rs 5,990 per ton over the fourth quarter helped offset the impact of lower volumes in India.
items.quote: We were able to offset the impact of the lower volumes because of an increase in the realisations to the tune of about Rs. 6,000 per ton, or Rs. 5,990 per ton to be more precise over 4Q.

items.statement: Chinese steel exports of 9 to 10 million tonnes a month and West Asian developments have impacted global steel supply chains and prices.
items.quote: The developments in West Asia continue to disrupt supply chains, and the Chinese steel exports of about 9 to 10 million tons a month have also had an impact on international prices.

items.statement: Conflict in West Asia caused unplanned consolidated cost increases of roughly Rs 1,200 crores through higher energy and logistics prices.
items.quote: It is important to emphasise that this is after the unplanned cost increases of about Rs. 1,200 crores on a consolidated basis due to the West Asia war. We have witnessed price spikes in energy prices

items.statement: The company expects cost pressures from the West Asia conflict to diminish in upcoming quarters through mitigation plans and alternative sourcing.
items.quote: With alternative sources and mitigation plans, we expect the impact to taper down in the coming quarters.

items.statement: positive
items.quote: But we expect volumes and EBITDA to be better in 2Q than 1Q, lower than what we would like it to be, but certainly starting to move in the right direction.
